newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open mostly unchanged on Monday, dealers said.
LIFFE is closed for a public holiday.

The Philippines will maintain its sugar export quota to the U.S., President Fidel Ramos, said. Last month, the Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration asked the president to order a stop to exports to the U.S., so it would not have to import sugar to meet its domestic needs.

Also, the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said output had reached 2.32 million tonnes by April 15, compared with 2.43 million tonnes for the same year-ago period. Stocks at mills are expected to last until the next sugarcane crushing season, which begins in October, the organization said.
The state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan will decide on a sugar tender on Wednesday. The tender was opened on Saturday as scheduled, but the company continues to negotiate with the bidders.
In India, sugar prices fell amid talk that the government may release extra sugar this month.
The French beet crop benefited from rain last week but more rainfall is needed to maintain growth after a three-month dry spell, analysts said.
Friday, most-active CSCE July closed 0.10 firmer at 10.80 cents per lb, having ranged from 10.82 to 10.65 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.07 higher to 0.02 weaker.
Support was seen at 10.25 cents in July while resistance was pegged at a gap on the charts between 10.86 and 10.92 cents.
((-- S Rostler New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
